title: 1971 AHSME Problem 14
statement: The number \(2^{48}-1\) is exactly divisible by two numbers between \(60\) and \(70.\) These numbers are:

solutions.text:
Because \(48\) is divisible by \(6,\) the number \[ 2^{48}-1 \] is divisible by \(63=2^6-1.\) Also \(2^{12}-1=4095=63\cdot65,\) and \(48\) is divisible by \(12,\) so \(2^{48}-1\) is divisible by \(65.\) Thus the two numbers are \(63\) and \(65.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use the fact that \(2^m-1\) divides \(2^n-1\) whenever \(n\) is divisible by \(m\)
Recognize \(63=2^6-1\) and that \(2^{12}-1\) is divisible by \(65\)
